sentences.text: Wellbore 15/9-F-1 C on Volve is a Sodir production wellbore with status P&A, and its reports run from 2014-02-21 to 2016-10-21.
There are 98 reports and the well duration is 973.96 days, which includes a long gap in reporting between the 2014 workover and the 2016 abandonment.
The deepest measured depth is 4094 m with a true vertical depth of 3180.5 m on the same report, and Sodir gives the same total depth of 4094 m.
Total activity time is 2220.25 h, of which primary lost time is 329.0 h, or 14.82 % of the activity time.
The outcome was three drilled hole sections to total depth, a completion and a workover in 2014, and a plug and abandonment campaign in 2016 that ended the well as P&A.
Sodir gives an entry date of 2014-02-21 and a completion date of 2014-03-18, which is the end of drilling, not production start-up.

That completion date matches the start of the completion phase, which begins on 2014-03-18 in the report-based sections, while the last report date of 2016-10-21 comes from the later abandonment work.
Section 1 is a 17.5 in section from 2014-02-21 to 2014-03-02, drilled from 1364 m to 2514 m with a true vertical depth of 2451.9 m at section end.
It drilled 1150 m of new hole at an average rate of 22.01 m/h while coded drilling -- drill, which is not an on-bottom rate of penetration.
Section 2 is a 12.25 in section from 2014-03-03 to 2014-03-10, drilled from 2517 m to 3059 m with a true vertical depth of 2874.4 m at section end.
It drilled 545 m of new hole at an average rate of 13.97 m/h while coded drilling -- drill, again not an on-bottom rate.
Section 3 is an 8.5 in section from 2014-03-11 to 2014-03-14, drilled from 3059 m to the total depth of 4094 m with a true vertical depth of 3180.5 m at section end.
It drilled 1035 m of new hole at an average rate of 19.26 m/h while coded drilling -- drill, not an on-bottom rate.

Sections 4 to 14 have an unknown hole size because the reports do not state one, they drilled no new hole, and their drilling rate is null because no time is coded drilling -- drill; the following sentences give their dates and depths.
Section 4 runs from 2014-03-15 to 2014-03-17 at a start depth of 4094 m and an end depth of 4094 m, true vertical depth 3180.5 m.
Section 5 (completion phase) runs from 2014-03-18 to 2014-03-21 at 4094 m, true vertical depth 3180.5 m.
Section 6 (completion phase) runs from 2014-03-22 to 2014-03-28 at 4094 m, true vertical depth 3180.5 m.
Section 7 (completion phase) runs from 2014-03-29 to 2014-04-02 at 4094 m, true vertical depth 3180.5 m.
Section 8 (completion phase) runs from 2014-04-03 to 2014-04-04 at 4094 m, true vertical depth 3180.5 m.
Section 9 (completion phase) runs from 2014-04-05 to 2014-04-06 at 4094 m, true vertical depth 3180.5 m.
Section 10 (completion phase) is a single-report section on 2014-04-07 at 4094 m, true vertical depth 3180.5 m.
Section 11 (completion phase) runs from 2014-04-08 to 2014-04-19 at 4094 m, true vertical depth 3180.5 m.
Section 12 (completion phase) runs from 2014-04-20 to 2014-04-21 at 4094 m, true vertical depth 3180.5 m.
Section 13 (workover phase) runs from 2014-11-27 to 2014-12-06; its start and end depths and true vertical depth are not reported in the section data.
Section 14 (plug and abandon phase) runs from 2016-06-15 to 2016-10-21 and ends at 4094 m with a true vertical depth of 3180.5 m.
Section 1 starts below a casing shoe at 1348.4 m and set casing with its shoe at 2507.7 m.
Section 2 starts below the shoe at 2507.7 m and set casing with its shoe at 3047.0 m.
Section 3 starts below the shoe at 3047.0 m and the tool reports no casing set in the section (shoe null).
Section 4 also starts below the shoe at 3047.0 m and reports no casing set.
From section 5 the deepest casing shoe is at 4087.1 m, so the casing run at the end of drilling is not attributed to any section by the tool, and none of sections 5 to 14 reports a casing set.
Sections 6 to 14 each start below the same shoe at 4087.1 m, shown here for section 6 and section 14.
Primary lost time over the wellbore is 329.0 h, or 14.82 % of the activity time, in 202 lost-time activities.
By cause, repair accounts for 186.0 h in 138 activities.
Waiting on weather accounts for 120.5 h in 46 activities.
Other waiting accounts for 18.25 h in 11 activities, and fishing for 4.25 h in 7 activities.
By section, section 1 (17.5 in) has 72.25 h primary lost time, 32.04 % of the section activity time, all of it waiting on weather.
Section 2 (12.25 in) has 9.75 h, or 5.08 %.
Section 3 (8.5 in) has 19.25 h, or 20.05 %.
Section 4 has 0.75 h, or 1.04 %.
Section 6 has 81.0 h, or 48.21 %, from waiting on weather, crane and rig repairs and other waiting.
Section 7 has 50.5 h, or 52.6 %, all repair.
Section 9 has 2.0 h, or 4.17 %.
Section 13 has 2.75 h, or 1.22 %.
Section 14 has 90.75 h, or 14.73 %, from repair, fishing and waiting.
Sections 5 and 11 have no primary lost time, and sections 8, 10 and 12 have no lost-time rows at all.
Possible lost time is reported separately and is not added to the primary figures: it totals 81.25 h, or 3.66 % of the activity time, in 78 activities.
Of this, the code interruption -- other makes up 79.75 h and maintain makes up 1.5 h.
The largest possible amounts are 27.5 h in section 11 (9.55 % of the section activity time) and 29.5 h in section 14 (4.79 %).

Waiting on weather started in the 17.5 in section on 2014-02-22, when cuttings could not be discharged to the supply vessel, forcing extra circulation, trips inside the previous shoe and rig maintenance, and it reached 72.25 h of primary lost time in that section.

On 2014-03-11 in the 8.5 in section the AutoTrak rotary steerable tool was diagnosed as faulty, the string was pulled to change the steering head, and the first troubleshooting step (coded possible lost time) took 2.25 h.
The trip and tool change were coded repair and, with other items, gave 19.25 h of primary lost time in that section.
Drilling reached the total depth of 4094 m in section 3 on 2014-03-14, ending the drilling phase.

From 2014-03-22 the completion phase waited on a weather window to disconnect and pull the riser equipment and then on a port crane brake and pump repair, including a 12.5 h repair block starting on 2014-03-25, and section 6 carries 81.0 h of primary lost time.
Reporting stops after 2014-12-06 and resumes on 2016-06-15 with the plug and abandonment campaign, so about the whole interval between is not covered by daily reports.
On 2016-06-19 the first wireline tubing cutter run came back with the cutter not fired, which cost 3.5 h coded as possible lost time, and a second run with a new cutter cut the tubing.
On 2016-06-26 a fishing job on a wellhead adapter tool needed a second spear run with a different spear type before the fish was pulled free, and fishing totals 4.25 h of primary lost time.

On 2016-06-29 the work string became stuck and could not be worked free by overpull and torque, leading to a 5.25 h evaluation, and the string was then cut by wireline after the crew waited for the cutting equipment to be mobilized while repairing the forward pipe racking system.

The difference between the Sodir completion date and the last report is explained by this later work: the 2014 completion date marks the end of drilling, while the 2016 reports cover tubing recovery, the stuck string and cementing before final abandonment.

Plan cuttings handling for bad weather on the next well, for example by having spare cuttings storage or a standby vessel, because waiting on weather totals 120.5 h of primary lost time, mostly in the 17.5 in section where cuttings could not be sent to the vessel.

Check and, where practical, run the rotary steerable and its downlink and gyro tools through shallow tests before the 8.5 in section, because a tool failure on 2014-03-11 led to a trip and 19.25 h of primary lost time in that section.

Service crane, pipe racking system and casing tong equipment before the completion and abandonment phases, because repair is the largest primary cause at 186.0 h and sections 6 and 7 lost 48.21 % and 52.6 % of their activity time.

For abandonment, have the wireline cutting equipment and a tested backup cutter on location before pulling tubing, because the stuck string on 2016-06-29 led to a long wait for cutting equipment and the first cutter run on 2016-06-19 did not fire.
Carry the right spear types and check the setting of retrieval tools before running them, as the fishing job on 2016-06-26 needed a second spear run.
Pressure test cementing lines and units before the job, since the 2016 cement spool and unit tests accounted for part of the possible lost time, which is kept separate from the primary figures.
Make sure the well is reported continuously, or document the long interval after 2014-12-06, so the well duration of 973.96 days can be separated into active and idle time.

row.comments: Waited one weather, not able to discharge cuttings to vessel due to bad weather.                           Circulated btm's up due to full iso tanks with 4000 lpm, 235 bar, 130-140 rpm, 3-6 kNm. ECD 1,43 SG. Max gas 0,02 %. Reciprocated pipe.

Established circulation and sent downlink. RIH to bottom and circulated with 2200 l/min. Baker performed diagnostics on downhole tools. Pulled into 9 5/8" shoe and continued troubleshooting on AutoTrak RSS.
Decided to POOH and change AutoTrak RSS.

Waited on Weather window (12 hrs) for disconnecting and pulling HPDR.
Meanwhile performed maintenance and started to change out wire on aft PRS.

Waited on Crane repair: Trouble shot problem with fluctating pressure on Port Crane emergency brake.
Started to change out pump.

Hoisted Tension joint above RKB. Closed spider and secured C-plates on top. Informed Production to start up at 13:00 hrs.

Meanwhile pressure tested TDS auto/man IBOP and Kelly hose to 20/345 bar for 5/10 min.
M/U RT for Production Riser to std and racked in derrick. Performed maintenance and derrick inspection.

Closed and inflow tested SV to 345 bar/10min.
B/O QTS.
L/O cutter toolstring on rig floor. Insptected same. Cutter had not fired.
GE and wellbore inspected tools. Wellbore tool found to be in release position due to LH turns in string to release well head adapter. Reset tool

Observed overpull when picking up work string between 138t and 300t on martin decker. String stuck @ 2362m.  Tried to work string free. Max pulled to 320t, max torque 40knm, sat down all string weight. No success to get string free. Evaluated further steps, started mobilizing WL cutter equipment to cut inside DP.
